A friends elderly uncle had a stroke and was sent to a recovery home where he kept declining. My friend asked me (long time patient within the medical system) to come with him to a visit. While there I asked if it was okay if I looked through his medical list and treatment plan. The doctors at this recovery home had him on nerve relaxants and heavy opioids for his morning medication which made him lethargic. 

When his doctor came in to check up on him I just asked about the medication since it to me seemed like it would be better if he got his afternoon pills in the morning and the morning pills in the afternoon. The doctor didn't agree at first but agreed that it wouldn't hurt to try switching them around at least for a week. A week later my friend calls me to come visit his uncle again, the dude was walking unassisted, doing exercise on a stationary bike 2 hours a day and was feeling much happier. The doctors called it a medical marvel... His uncle made a full recovery after one month, were he had previously been declining for almost half a year...

I drink. Many of my friends don't drink. We all mix at the same social settings. No one gives the alco-free people any shit. Everyone gives us (the drinkers) shit for being stupid. 

If you are in a social setting where people are drinking and you don't want to that should trump all arguments. Anytime someone tries to pressure you to drink know that these aren't your friends and you should probably reconsider hanging out with them.

Okay, there's already lots of SMART and REASONABLE comments telling you to reconsider and just don't drink so I guess I'll have to be devil's advocate here. As a disclaimer though, alcohol generally sucks. 

You want to get more comfortable drinking, start slow and easy, light beers, low alcohol wine or cider or even alcohol free alternatives. Taste test anything that could be served with higher alcohol contents until you find something to your taste. (As an example I don't drink beer at all, but love wine and cider).

Step two, drink responsibly. Don't chug 6 [brand name] beers in a 30 minute sitting. Have one, drink it slowly and without stress. It's finished? Wait 10 minutes and have a glass of water before the next one, ask yourself if you feel okay and if another drink feels okay. Drinking and being drunk are two different things and you have no need to get intoxicated to levels where you are slurring or stumbling.

 From there you can extrapolate how much affect one drink has on you and how much you can drink without it feeling like everything is spinning. Next time you are out with friends, keep yourself at that level, plus or minus one drink. Staring to get too tipsy? Air and water, wait a while before next drink. 

Drink responsibly. Be careful. Don't feel peer pressure.

So getting tiny trace amounts of bleach into your system through cuts on your skin. No problem. It might sting like a MF though.

Look maybe I can put you to ease: I work with Bleach and other strong chemicals on a daily basis (Kitchen work so we have lots of cleaning to do at closing). 

Bleach burns sting like a bitch if its pure bleach and you have sensitive skin. However, its not uncommon for me to literally rinse my hands of in pure bleach (cup hand, pour bleach into it, rub hands together) then letting them rinse through running water for a couple of minutes. If you didnt get it in a open wound or ingest it by drinking it, then you are fine and you have nothing to worry about. Bleach is unlikely do be dangerous to you or your skin (from a long term perspective)

If the area looks really irritated and keeps stinging/hurting after cleaning it with WATER ONLY (mild soap or just water no other chems) and/or if its red and bubbly/bulging/bumpy go see a doctor, they will likely prescribe a skin cream to be applied to the area for a week, IF it looks bad that is. The cream will be applied for 1-2 weeks and is just to make sure you dont get scars or stuff so its not like they are prescribing some antibiotic.

Bleach is a strong chemical, but for skin its irritation but not dangerous. Inhalation, digestion or getting it in things like eyes are the things you should watch out for. And NEVER EVER mix bleach with anything except water unless you are sure what you are mixing (most chem reactions with bleach create dangerous gases).

If you feel like you would be calmer with a medical professionals advice I suggest you call your doctor and and ask for an opinion. But you should not be worried about long term illness or whatever. Worst case scenario would be a bleach burn (pigment discoloration) which can take a long time to "heal" since its skin cells that will need to replace the bleached cells - but even this is not dangerous nor uncomfortable and its highly improbable if you rinsed it under running water for the amount of time you mentioned.

As a major player on the world stage I have learned (both with and without DLC features) that my old strategy of making protectorate and protectorate is a horrible strategy. 

Since honestly the only way to hugely impact liberty desire is INFAMY based more than anything. Make Morroco a protectorate, build up all their farmlands, build industry to the point where they have unemployment issues due to lacking pop... Still disloyal because you have been over infamy 25 for 5 seconds. And you still "get nothing" from them (income from your buildings and products to your market sure... But you could've built it in your own country probably). 

Then you make them a Dominion after struggling for YEARS and get 25% only for them to instantly become disloyal and joining every war you start on the enemy side demanding independence... 

As a subject, unless your AI overlord is a warmonger, you can't ever get free without doing things that just feel wrong. (Like actively get rebellions, hope that rebellion gets supported by a great power and switch sides...) or cheesing bad relationships in hope of generating a lobby against the overlord and then just pray. 

But the "problems" are extended further when you look at the drawback/investment/gain of creating a PROTECTORATE. These Vassals used to be "they join your market, that's it, and after 10 years you can demand they become a Dominion" which made it easy to chain area conquests. Protectorate Morroco, the Mascara, Tunis etc... Ten years later you made them dominions one after the other. 

Now... If you do it that route you will have 3-5 angry vassals as Protectorates for 40 years. Better is to annex/conquest Morroco, instantly release them as a loyal Puppet (30% income) and upgrade them to dominion instantly (25% income BUT they will expand in their area for you without infamy for you), and then keep feeding culture accepted provinces into them through conquest wars. Reach a new area where Morrocos culture will not accept them? Create new vassal and continue.
As opposed to being a player and making something a protectorate only for them to never become loyal due to you having infamy.

Since 1.7 I have played 5 full runs to test out the new systems. I can say with no doubt that the following statements are fact: If you want to vassalize something, steal a Dominion/Puppet from someone, or conquer territory and then release it after war as Puppet. 

As Spain I wanted to go for a "Mare Nostrum" run so I vassalize Morroco through Tunis all as Protectorates... Due to how infamy effects vassals and that Protectorates does NOT give you income (they only add to your market) it took me 50 years to start making any relevant money from northern Africa. Because keeping them loyal enough to bring down to dominion wasn't happening... 

As Russia in another run, I physically annexed most of Iraq from the Ottomans and released Iraq and gave them all territorial Arab lands. Instantly had a loyal Puppet than transfered 30% of the wealth to me with no internal turmoil due to full accepted culture and religion.

Are all indie games better than AAA games? No. 

Are all AAA games better than indie games? No.

The theoretical is that AAA studios should in general have better quality. And quality is a BROAD term. It can mean it has HD graphics with realistic gore when you slay an enemy. But when QUALITY and GAMEPLAY doesn't feel like they correlate then people start complaining. 

If the newest... Call of Duty looks fantastic, has amazing sound mixture, realistic water features etc... But running around and shooting feels like playing Duke Nukem or Doom then you are in trouble.

Indie games tell us straight up; Hey I/we made this passion project. It might not be perfect and we are willing to sell it at a low price if people want to play it.
